draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Vythiri! Just up the road at Lakkidi, a chain hangs from a tree, and there's a ghost story behind it. Wayanad is one of the rainiest places in Kerala.
draft.hungryLine: Wayanad eats bamboo rice, chicken curry and lots of coffee. Here's where to start.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Stop at the Lakkidi viewpoint, see the chain tree, then go boating on Pookode Lake.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Paddle around Pookode Lake and listen to the forest.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The road up to Wayanad has nine hairpin bends. People call it the Thamarassery churam.

legends.title: The ghost in chains
legends.body: Karinthandan, a tribal man, is said to have guided a British engineer up this pass. The engineer killed him to take the credit. His restless spirit was chained to this tree.

legends.title: A lake shaped like a map
legends.body: Locals say Pookode Lake, seen from above, is shaped a bit like India.

tips.title: Pack a raincoat.
tips.body: Wayanad rains are heavy from June to September.

tips.title: Buy coffee and spices from farms.
tips.body: Wayanad grows coffee, pepper and cardamom.

story.title: Forest people
story.body: Wayanad's hills have been home to tribal communities like the Paniya and the Kurichiya for centuries.

story.title: Carved in stone
story.body: At Edakkal, south of here, people carved figures into cave walls thousands of years ago.

story.title: A pass through the ghats
story.body: The British built a road up the steep pass at Lakkidi to reach the Wayanad plateau.

story.title: Coffee and tea
story.body: Planters cleared land for coffee, tea and pepper, which still cover the hills.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Lakkidi view, the chain tree, then a boat on Pookode Lake. Tell me if you felt the ghost.
